title: Two chairs
logline: Christmas Eve, 2026. Gully's dock, string lights. Maria's lawn chair, and beside it a second chair, folding, set out. Both empty. Whether she comes is not this page's; the second chair is.

margin.note: The crab, small, beside the word.

panels.composition: The dock at night with string lights, Christmas Eve: Maria's old lawn chair and, set carefully beside it, a second chair — a folding one, the one from August 2024 — both empty, both facing the water. Snow not falling but threatening. The shack's window warm. Somebody set out two chairs.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a wooden dock at night strung with lights on Christmas Eve, an old worn lawn chair and a folding chair set carefully side by side facing the water both empty, a shingle shack's window glowing warm, a heavy sky, no people, no words
image.notes: Reserved whether she comes. Two chairs is the page's whole statement.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: Two chairs, empty, facing the water. Set out by someone.
